A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TriSense and TriSense-2M. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching across relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning, moment-retrieval, and VideoMME evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative case studies, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds experiments on slot compression, prediction heads, and connector branches in Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: v1 Section 4.2, Equation 4, and Algorithm 2 specify weighted summation of modality features. v3 replaces this with weighted concatenation followed by additional slot compression before the two-layer MLP. This substantively changes the specified operation of the central Query-Based Connector.

E1.justification: Training datasets and task coverage remain unchanged. Both versions evaluate TriSense-2M, LongVALE, Charades-STA, ActivityNet-Captions, and VideoMME. LongVALE moves from the appendix to the main text; the new ablations vary model configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: External baseline membership remains unchanged in corresponding benchmark comparisons. v3 adds controlled comparison variants within its supplementary experiments: a Unified Head alternative and V-only, VS-only, and AV-only connector branches, compared with the two-head and full-AVS designs in Tables 13–15.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces a supplementary protocol using 20K randomly selected samples, three training epochs, 64-frame sampling, and TRACE initialization; branch ablations additionally specify a frozen LLM backbone. Existing benchmark metrics, test-subset selection, and principal training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial component analyses: 8/16/32/64-slot compression, unified versus separate prediction heads, and removal of modality branches across captioning and retrieval tasks (Tables 12–15). The earlier training-stage, weighting, and frame-count ablations remain, as do all six case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for model performance. The new ablations continue reporting individual point estimates; their random sample selection is an experimental-design detail.

E6.justification: Tables 12–15 add substantial numerical evidence under the new small-scale protocol. For example, Table 13 reports AVS-captioning CIDEr of 1.1 versus 2.4 and retrieval R@0.5 of 0.2 versus 0.4 for unified versus separate heads. Existing benchmark scores, earlier ablation values, and case-study outputs remain unchanged after relocation.

T1.justification: Equation 4 changes the mathematical definition of the fused representation from an MLP applied to a weighted sum to an MLP applied to compressed, concatenated weighted features. Other mathematical formulations remain unchanged; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: query-adaptive multimodal fusion, flexible modality handling, the long-video TriSense-2M dataset, and strong captioning and retrieval performance. The added analyses do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations about compression tradeoffs, time-head benefits, and modality contributions. It removes v1's captioning-specific spatial-redundancy explanation and generalizes the approximately 50% Stage-2 capability statement to both tasks. Its new full-AVS superiority interpretation is not uniform across metrics: Table 14 reports V-SC BLEU of 1.0 for V-only versus 0.8 for full AVS.

D1.justification: v3 removes Appendix C.3's connector pseudocode, including positional-encoding, normalization, residual, and temperature details. It adds a repository pointer, detailed event/test-set statistics, and supplementary training recipes. Training documentation also becomes inconsistent: Table 11 changes Stage-3 duration from seven to 5.5 days, while Appendix A.3 still states seven days.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 38 reference entries and the same related-work discussion and research positioning. Reference back-pointer changes reflect pagination, without adding or removing cited research.

P1.justification: The bulk of the narrative remains unchanged. Local restructuring moves LongVALE discussion and captioning ablations into Section 5.2, revises appendix subsection organization, and removes the pseudocode subsection. v3 also adds acknowledgements, updates the venue line, and makes limited wording corrections.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands quantitative displays with dataset/test-set statistics and four component-ablation tables. It relocates existing LongVALE and captioning-ablation tables, updates Figure 4 for concatenation and compression, and removes both algorithm displays. Table 12 introduces mismatched column headings, although its metric-labelled entries remain interpretable.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations and dataset statistics improve architectural scrutiny and evaluation transparency. However, v3 changes the central fusion operation while retaining headline scores without clarifying their relationship to that revision, removes detailed connector pseudocode, and introduces conflicting training-time information. The PDFs leave unresolved whether the methodological revision corrects documentation or changes the model underlying those results, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
